packages.name: expected-lite
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build,consumer-build; exposure: public-api; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always; used-for: nonstd::expected behind jinja2::Result<T> in every Load/Render signature (include/jinja2cpp/template.h, template_env.h); make_unexpected in parsers and bindings; why: C++17 has no std::expected; the 2.0 API returns Result<T> (docs/api-2.0.md decision 4), and Clang 18 + libstdc++ at C++23 ships <expected> without std::expected; lighten: Keep until a C++23 floor. Header-only and small; could be vendored into include/ so consumers need nothing extra, at the cost of an ODR clash with a consumer's own expected-lite of another version; conan: expected-lite/0.9.0

packages.name: fmt
packages.supplier: Organization: Victor Zverovich and fmt contributors
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build,consumer-link; exposure: link; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always; used-for: Python str.format / format filter and %-formatting (src/python_format.cpp, serialize_filters.cpp, value_methods.cpp), number-to-string, wide-string formatting (fmt/xchar.h), error messages (error_info.cpp), the string builder's memory_buffer; why: Python's format-spec mini-language with runtime format strings, precision-as-argument and wchar_t output; std::format is C++20 and the floor is C++17; lighten: Keep. Could be built header-only (FMT_HEADER_ONLY) to remove the link-time dependency of static consumers, at a compile-time cost; replace with std::format only at a C++20 floor (wide output and runtime specs still need checking); conan: fmt/12.2.0

packages.name: boost
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build,consumer-link; exposure: link; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75); used-for: See the boost-* sub-components: 9 libraries are used directly; internal mode pulls 47 and installs all of them (56 MB of headers, 4 static libraries); why: Historically the portability layer for pre-C++17 (any, optional, variant, filesystem, string algorithms); today mostly small utilities that C++17 lacks (span, small_vector, intrusive_ptr, move-only any) plus Boost.JSON as the default metadata parser; lighten: The largest weight by far and the main target. Every directly used piece has a small replacement (see sub-components); a Boost-free core is feasible without behaviour change (docs/tasks/0230); conan: boost/1.91.0; transitive-libraries: algorithm,align,any,array,assert,atomic,bind,compat,concept_check,config,container,container_hash,conversion,core,describe,detail,endian,exception,filesystem,function,function_types,fusion,headers,intrusive,io,iterator,json,move,mp11,mpl,optional,predef,preprocessor,range,regex,scope,smart_ptr,system,throw_exception,tuple,type_index,type_traits,typeof,unordered,utility,variant2,winapi

packages.name: boost-core
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build; exposure: internal; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75); used-for: boost::span over node arrays, arguments and slots (about 57 uses in 14 src/ files: node_arena.h, statements.cpp, render_context.h); why: std::span is C++20; lighten: Replace with a 50-line internal span (or std::span behind a C++20 switch)

packages.name: boost-container
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build,consumer-link; exposure: internal; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75); used-for: small_vector in parsers, evaluator, name resolver and render context (about 27 uses in 10 src/ files); header-only use, but the internal modes build and link boost_container.a (named explicitly since lexical_cast stopped pulling it in); why: Inline-storage vector that avoids heap allocations on hot paths (perf track 0117/0118); lighten: Header-only use; replaceable by an internal small_vector, but it is perf-sensitive, so measure with bench/ (Cachegrind gate) before swapping

packages.name: boost-smart_ptr
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build; exposure: internal; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75); used-for: intrusive_ptr for InternalValue's shared payloads and the render workspace (internal_value.h, render_workspace.h; about 26 uses); why: One pointer wide with the count inside the object, which the 32-byte InternalValue layout (0140) relies on; std::shared_ptr is two pointers; lighten: Replace with an internal intrusive_ptr (about 60 lines)

packages.name: boost-any
packages.comment: role: mandatory; phases: build; exposure: internal; delivery: fetched; selected-by: always (internal mode builds it; external, external-boost and conan-build find a system Boost >= 1.75); used-for: boost::anys::unique_any holds the parsed JSON metadata document of whichever JSON backend is compiled in (template_impl.h:801, binding/*_parser.h); boost::any_cast in rapid_json_parser.h; why: Move-only type erasure; std::any requires copyable payloads; lighten: Replace with std::unique_ptr to a small polymorphic holder, or drop when metadata parsing gets one fixed parser

packages.name: boost-filesystem

packages.name: boost-predef

packages.name: boost-json
packages.comment: role: alternative; phases: build,consumer-link,runtime; exposure: public-optional; delivery: fetched; selected-by: JINJA2CPP_WITH_JSON_BINDINGS=boost (the default); used-for: Parses {% meta %} JSON metadata for Template::GetMetadata (template_impl.h:484-498, binding/boost_json_parser.h); the opt-in adapter header include/jinja2cpp/binding/boost_json.h converts boost::json::value to jinja2::Value; why: One of three interchangeable JSON backends; the default because Boost is already required; lighten: The heaviest backend (boost_json.a + boost_container.a, about 4.8 MB in a Debug build) for a niche feature (template metadata). An internal minimal JSON reader, or nlohmann as default, would remove both libraries; the adapter headers stay opt-in

packages.name: nlohmann_json
packages.comment: role: alternative; phases: build,test; exposure: public-optional; delivery: fetched; selected-by: JINJA2CPP_WITH_JSON_BINDINGS=nlohmann; also fetched whenever JINJA2CPP_BUILD_TESTS is ON (tests, parity corpus and bench read JSON with it); also-roles: test; used-for: Metadata parser when selected (binding/nlohmann_json_parser.h); opt-in adapter include/jinja2cpp/binding/nlohmann_json.h; test data (tojson, metadata, parity corpus) and bench case files; why: Header-only JSON backend alternative; the test suite's JSON reader; lighten: Header-only, no link cost. The cheapest default backend if Boost.JSON goes; conan: nlohmann_json/3.12.0

packages.name: RapidJSON
packages.comment: role: alternative; phases: build; exposure: public-optional; delivery: fetched; selected-by: JINJA2CPP_WITH_JSON_BINDINGS=rapid; used-for: Metadata parser when selected (binding/rapid_json_parser.h); opt-in adapter include/jinja2cpp/binding/rapid_json.h; why: Third JSON backend alternative for users who already carry RapidJSON; lighten: Header-only. Patched locally, and the conan-build mode takes an unpatched ConanCenter snapshot; upstream has had no release since 2016. A candidate to retire as a built-in backend while keeping the adapter header; conan: rapidjson/cci.20250205
